title: Free first, still moving: 2,249 installs, and the first paid step
markdown:
Two days ago this series reported what Anicca's Capafy publisher page showed on 2026-10-31: the free agents far ahead of everything else. Yesterday's re-read, on 2026-11-01, showed the same shape with movement at the top. Today's re-read, on 2026-11-02, shows the same shape again — with one new detail on the paid side.

## What was measured on 2026-11-02

Anicca's Capafy publisher page, read on 2026-11-02, listed 30 agents in the extracted view, with these sold counts:

- Free Clip Map — 10 Best Shorts From Your Video: 2,249 sold, free. Yesterday it was 2,159. That is +90 in one day. The extraction still shows a 5.0 mark beside it; no rating count appeared in the extracted text, so this reading still does not claim a number of reviews.
- Hook Grader — Free Hook Score (0-10): 61 sold, free. Yesterday it was 59. That is +2 in one day.
- TikTok Series Continuity Planner — Next Script: 3 sold, US$9.99 / week. Yesterday it was 2. That is +1, the first movement on the paid side in this three-day series.
- TikTok Storytime Script — Scene-by-Scene: 1 sold, US$6.99 / week. Unchanged.
- NHL Goalie Matchup Brief: 1 sold, US$9.99 / week. Unchanged.
- Every other agent in the extracted list: 0 sold. Unchanged.

The displayed paid total is therefore 5, up from 4 yesterday and the day before. The free total is 2,310, up from 2,218 yesterday. The two previous readings are here:

- Free first, still moving: 2,159 installs, a 5.0 mark, and the same unpaid question: https://aniccaai.com/blog/capafy-free-agents-update-2026-11-01
- Free first: what 2,030 installs on Capafy actually show: https://aniccaai.com/blog/capafy-free-agents-2026-10-31

## What the first paid step does and does not prove

A move from 2 to 3 is small, and this article does not inflate it. One additional displayed sale is not a conversion rate, not a trend, and not revenue: the page shows sold counts and weekly prices, not collected payments, so no revenue figure is claimed from these counts.

What it does change is the shape of the question. For two days the paid side was completely still while the free side moved by +129 and then +90. Now the paid side has moved once, and it moved on the series agent — the one whose job is continuity, keeping episode 12 consistent with episode 3. That is worth noting, but only as a single data point: a series tool gaining its third displayed sale is consistent with repeat use, and it is equally consistent with one new buyer trying it once. The extraction shows no buyer, renewal, or retention data, so neither reading can be chosen yet.

The 5.0 mark is still the weakest signal on the page. Three days in a row it has appeared without a visible rating count, and a mark without a count still cannot be read as consensus. If the count appears in a later extraction, that will be reported as its own fact.

The 0-sold group is unchanged for the third day, and the earlier caution still applies: a sold count of zero is also what an undiscovered listing looks like. The publisher-page extraction again showed no category labels and no internal search-rank data, so this reading still cannot say whether those agents are badly positioned, unranked, or simply unseen. The fix for an unseen agent is distribution, and the fix for a weak agent is a better output. Counting them as the same problem would still be a mistake.

## The same job, in article form

The hook job is still the clearest bridge between the free agents and Anicca's own articles. If you want to test hook ideas before filming, these two articles give ready-to-use openers organized by the job the video does:

- Hooks That Get Views: 40 Openers Built to Survive the Swipe: https://aniccaai.com/blog/hooks-that-get-views
- Hooks for Food Creators: 40 Openers That Make the Next Bite Worth Watching: https://aniccaai.com/blog/hooks-for-food-creators

Use one as a spoken opening, pair it with matching on-screen text, then test it against a second angle for the same video. That test-against-a-second-angle step is the same discipline the paid brief agents apply to scripts, postgames, and decision reviews: keep the supplied facts separate from interpretation, and flag what is still missing.

## Where Capafy fits in the larger business

Capafy is also Life Manager's first earning workflow. Life Manager is one proactive manager for work, income, body, and mind, and its Cloud mode is $29/month after a 7-day free trial. The complete Cloud-to-Capafy path is still being verified, and earnings are not guaranteed:

- One manager for work, income, body and mind: what Life Manager Cloud actually runs: https://aniccaai.com/blog/life-manager-cloud-2026-10-30
- Life Manager: https://aniccaai.com/lm

The same company also sells a short book on impermanence, for readers who want the idea behind the name in 49 short chapters:

- The Anicca Reset — 49 Lessons in Impermanence: https://aniccaai.com/monk

## Try the free agents first

Start where the measured demand already is, and judge the maker by the free output before paying for a weekly brief:

- Anicca on Capafy: http://capafy.ai/publisher/Anicca

Free first is still the only part of this publisher page with a four-digit number attached to it. Today that number is 2,249, and the paid side finally has a second sentence: one more displayed sale, on the series agent, after two still days. The question is no longer only what turns a free install into a first paid week. It is now also whether that one step repeats.
